Wisconsin Creative · Web + iOS · October 22, 2026

Onboarding that continues with you

Account-backed setup, optional photo completion, and direct photo gestures. Current local evidence for the six-student onboarding rollout.

Browser recovery

7 passed

Real component interactions with fixture APIs.

Database continuity

8 passed

Disposable PostgreSQL; no hosted student account.

Native runtime

10 + 2 passed

Model/image XCTest plus two iPhone 18 Pro Max UI scenarios.

Move the photo itself

After-only evidence. No sliders. A circular guide preserves photo context; iOS uses native pan/pinch and web supports drag, pinch, scroll and keyboard controls. Technical fixture images are used instead of student photos.

An interrupted upload keeps your crop

The simulated server failure remains visible. Retry reuses the selected framing; upload bytes are checked against the selected off-center preview region.

Saved answers and explicit conflict recovery

Valid field groups save to the account; incomplete private text stays in memory and is shown as unsaved. Changes elsewhere never silently overwrite local edits.

Photo is optional; Finish is durable

Both clients send FINISH after required information is complete, including when no photo is selected. A persisted completion receipt prevents a future session from reopening Welcome for the missing photo.

What changed, and why

Direct photo gestures

Was

Separate sliders controlled zoom and each movement axis.

Now

The image is the interaction surface. System pan/pinch on iOS and drag/pinch/scroll on web keep the photo under direct control.

Account-backed continuation

Was

Complete-step writes and photo-dependent completion could make interrupted setup or skipped photos ambiguous.

Now

Validated field groups, explicit conflict choices and a durable Finish receipt keep the saved state and completion decision separate.

Safer photo replacement

Was

A request could be interrupted or arrive after another device changed the photo.

Now

Frozen photo/account versions and upload IDs reject stale replacements and reconcile confirmed uploads. The old image is deleted only after the new pointer and audit commit.

Verification

  • TypeScript and app build pass. Lint reports 0 errors; existing repository warnings remain. The crop editor and changed browser test lint cleanly.
  • Focused API, profile, avatar, image and audit-inventory tests pass. Disposable PostgreSQL covers partial saves, contention, replay, rollback, legacy compatibility and photo-free FINISH.
  • All 780 native source-contract tests pass across 148 files. Native target build and 10 model/image XCTest cases pass, including distinctive off-center crop pixels.
  • Both final iPhone 18 Pro Max UI scenarios pass: actual pinch/drag with retained crop on failure, and the required student sequence through photo skip and Finish.
  • Xcode project registration, schema validation, 201 migration-prefix checks, docs/codemaps and diff whitespace checks pass.
  • Mobbin MCP connected and queried successfully. WHOOP, Me+ and Tripadvisor references informed the circular guide, image context and brief guidance. Their stills establish layout/copy, not live gesture behavior.

Things to know

  • These are current fixture captures with no trustworthy matched pre-change baseline; no before/after size or performance measurement is claimed. Older slider captures in this folder are superseded.
  • Authenticated web-to-iOS and iOS-to-web handoff remains pending. D-063 requires this branch’s own Managed preview, obtained after an authorized scoped commit, push and draft PR. No branch environment is currently available.
  • Physical iPhone photo-library/permission behavior and shared-backend avatar display remain pending. Simulator and fixture proof do not establish those device/backend outcomes.
  • Migration 0200 has not been deployed. No commit, push, PR, production mutation, deployment, email or distribution has occurred.
  • Source snapshot, per-file hashes, capture hashes and passing logs are retained alongside this page. Native Swift source in the installed private test snapshot was verified byte-identical; only bundle/app-group identity differs intentionally.
  • The browser refused the local file protocol, so the review page was not browser-rendered here. Its HTML structure, embedded images, alt text and every selected source image were inspected directly; Codex queued the local file for viewing.
